sampling_model.design: The design algebra fixes any finite binary-path support \(\mathcal S\) and a positive ex ante reshaping law \(\Pi\); absorption is required only for the ordered Green, graph-rank, and adjacent-ratio corollaries.
sampling_model.units: The base causal-identification layer is a conditional-mean superpopulation model.  A separate unit-indexed, possibly dependent triangular-array layer contains the published Arkhangelsky--Imbens--Lei--Luo class exactly after taking the reshaping support to be their \(\mathcal S^*\); its maximal-correlation condition yields the sharp coefficient approximation rate \(O_P(n^{-q/2})\).  No inclusion relation between this published layer and the base superpopulation class is used.
sampling_model.treatment: In the base algebra, \(W_i\) may be any path in the declared finite binary support.  Ordered adoption-time results explicitly restrict that support to absorbing paths.
sampling_model.overlap: The population layer assumes \(\pi_s(X)\geq c_{\pi}\) and \(\Pi_s\geq\epsilon\).  The published layer instead uses known unit-specific propensities \(\pi_i(s)\geq c_*\) on the reshaping support and defines its RIPW weight to be zero off that support.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The population functional uses a correct common generalized path propensity and pathwise conditional means.  The anchor-faithful statistical theorem is for the published known-propensity estimator; it does not assert a cross-fitted or doubly robust extension.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Arkhangelsky, Imbens, Lei, and Luo establish homogeneous dynamic RIPW consistency under their unit-indexed known-propensity setup and Assumptions 2.1--2.3.  The matched theorem works in exactly that sampling layer upon taking the reshaping support to be their \(\mathcal S^*\), extends the coefficient approximation to calendar-varying finite-memory effects at rate \(O_P(n^{-q/2})\), and proves by a block construction that those assumptions alone imply no uniformly faster coefficient rate; the separate base superpopulation class is incomparable with the published class.
A conventional event-study lag coefficient is a weighted average of cohort effects from its own and other relative periods.
Inverse-probability estimators of finite-memory dynamic effects are unbiased under known panel randomization, with finite-population limit theory.
Under a time-constant random-coefficient distributed-lag model, average lag coefficients can be identified in complex treatment designs.
Conventional staggered event-study regressions admit computable probability-limit diagnostics for negative weights and cross-horizon contamination.
A time-varying parameter distributed-lag model permits lag coefficients to vary with past information.

body.tldr: For any finite binary-path support, the base superpopulation layer gives an exact reshaped distributed-lag loading tensor, covariance and pair-mass formulas, normalization, and exact rational diagnostics.  That layer is incomparable with the published class.  A separate unit-indexed triangular-array layer contains the Arkhangelsky--Imbens--Lei--Luo class exactly upon taking the reshaping support to be their \(\mathcal S^*\): there the published weighted regression has tensor approximation rate \(O_P(n^{-q/2})\), homogeneous effects recover their Theorem \(4.1\) directly, and a block construction shows that Assumptions 2.1--2.3 alone imply no uniformly faster coefficient rate.  An independently randomized three-period witness belongs to a published-class subclass, so failure of calendar-homogeneous reduction transfers to the larger calendar-varying published layer.  For absorbing supports, graph connectivity gives the exact rank dimension and adjacent ratios give a pointwise Cramer certificate; global sign-chamber enumeration remains open.

project_justification.gap: Published RIPW theory establishes dynamic consistency under calendar-homogeneous effects and explicitly leaves its time-varying DATE equation beyond scope.  Its unit-indexed known-propensity class permits arbitrary binary paths, non-identical units, weak cross-unit dependence, and unit-specific effects, whereas the base conditional-mean superpopulation layer imposes different restrictions; the two classes are incomparable, so homogeneous recovery cannot be transferred by class inclusion.  Existing results also do not give the present sharp \(q\)-dependent calendar-loading approximation, absorbing graph-rank law, or exact fixed-law sign certificate.
project_justification.niche: The missing objects are an arbitrary-path forward loading tensor shared across two clearly separated sampling layers, plus sharp ordered diagnostics that use absorption only where it is mathematically necessary.
project_justification.fill: The project first proves arbitrary-path covariance and pair-mass identities, exact normalization, and rational diagnostics in the base superpopulation layer.  It then analyzes a separate unit-indexed triangular-array layer that contains the published class exactly when its reshaping support is their \(\mathcal S^*\): the calendar-varying tensor approximation is \(O_P(n^{-q/2})\), homogeneous recovery is direct in that layer, and a two-period block construction certifies that no uniformly faster coefficient rate follows from Assumptions 2.1--2.3 alone.  An independently randomized three-period counterexample lies in a published-class subclass and therefore transfers nonreduction upward.  Positive-law absorbing graph geometry and a pointwise adjacent-ratio Cramer certificate are proved, while global sign chambers remain open.

body.related_work: Arkhangelsky, Imbens, Lei, and Luo (2024) allow arbitrary binary-path support, unit-specific known generalized propensities conditional on full potential-outcome schedules, non-identical units, and weak cross-unit dependence.  The separate unit-indexed theorem contains that published class exactly upon setting the reshaping support to their \(\mathcal S^*\), retains the grand intercept in their equation \(4.2\), extends the coefficient approximation to calendar-varying finite-memory effects at rate \(O_P(n^{-q/2})\), and directly recovers their Theorem \(4.1\) under homogeneity.  Its block witness proves that Assumptions 2.1--2.3 alone yield no uniformly faster coefficient rate.  The base conditional-mean superpopulation class is incomparable with the published class and supplies no inclusion argument.  Moreover, the independently randomized three-period nonreduction witness lies in a published-class subclass, so its failure of calendar-homogeneous reduction transfers upward.  Sun and Abraham (2021) decompose conventional event-study coefficients but do not study assignment-law reshaping of finite-memory lag regressors.  Bojinov, Rambachan, and Shephard (2021) motivate treatment-history indexing under known experimental assignment.  De Chaisemartin and D'Haultfoeuille (2025) recover time-constant random-coefficient distributed lags in complex designs.  Wright (2026) supplies adjacent public-manuscript evidence on conventional event-study diagnostics, and Ailigeng, Lu, and Wang (2023) supply modeling precedent for time-varying distributed-lag coefficients; none supplies the present tensor, sharp published-layer rate, and ordered support geometry.
body.honest_scope: The proved forward algebra covers arbitrary finite binary-path supports.  Causal identification in the base superpopulation layer requires consistency, pathwise conditional mean random assignment, overlap, the stated calendar-memory conditional mean, and full rank; this layer is incomparable with the published class.  The separate unit-indexed triangular-array theorem contains the Arkhangelsky--Imbens--Lei--Luo class exactly when the reshaping support is their \(\mathcal S^*\), retains their known unit-specific propensities and maximal-correlation condition, and proves the sharp uniform coefficient approximation rate \(O_P(n^{-q/2})\).  The randomized three-period witness is in a published-class subclass, so its calendar-varying nonreduction conclusion transfers upward.  Absorption is used only for the Green-kernel identity, graph-rank theorem, and adjacent-ratio certificate.  The graph dimension formula requires every reshaping mass to be positive and is false at the simplex boundary without deleting zero-mass paths.  The adjacent-ratio result is pointwise: no global sign-chamber enumeration, inverse-image optimization, certified closest loading, or worst-case contamination optimization is claimed.  No central limit theorem, asymptotic normality, or cross-fitted doubly robust result is claimed.
